LESSON: PROGRAM DEVELOPMENT OVERVIEW

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: COMPUTER STUDIES FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Software development
Topic 3.2: Program development overview
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 18

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Program development overview, part of Software development in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 COMPUTER STUDIES FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: How are programs developed? 2. Why are algorithms designed?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Program development overview together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Creativity and Imagination: the learner undertakes tasks while working on a problem to find a solution by constructing an

algorithm using a flowchart and pseudocode.

• Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: the learner seeks alternative ways of using algorithms in problem solving.

50

Values:
● Respect is enhanced as learners understand and appreciate others as they discuss the significance of algorithms in problem

solving.

● Integrity is enhanced as the learner displays honesty when participating in a group activity involving the drawing and

discussion of symbols in a program flowchart.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Socio-Economic and Environmental Issues: the learner enhances road safety by writing an algorithm on how traffic lights

operate.

Suggested resources:

● Computer Software (Operating System and Application Program)

● Audio/visual clip

● Screen Reader

● Magnifier

● Headphone

● Manilla papers

● Braille papers

● Permanent marker pen

● Human Resources (teachers, computer laboratory technicians).

Suggested key skills:

● Writing pseudo codes to illustrate the logical flow of an algorithm.

● Representing the logical flow of an algorithm using a flow chart.
